description_full: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ), together with its subsidiaries, provides mobile connectivity solutions to communications service providers, enterprises, and the public sector in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Northeast Asia, Southeast Asia, Oceania, and India. It operates through Networks; Cloud Software and Services; Enterprise; and Other segments. The Networks segment offers hardware, software, and service offerings for intelligent, reliable and flexible 5G networks. This segment also provides energy-efficient RAN with an AI-native software architecture deployable on Ericsson silicon and third-party CPUs/GPUs; transport networks; and active/ passive antennas, as well as deployment and lifecycle management services. The Cloud Software and Services segment provides core networks, network management, business and operations support systems, and network operations delivered as managed services, including secure data and voice connectivity, service monetization and orchestration tools, and network management services. The Enterprise segment offers intelligent networking and advanced communications software solutions comprising global communications platform, wireless wide area networks (WWAN), and private 5G networks. The Other segment includes RedBee Media that prepares and distributes live and on-demand video services for broadcasters, sports leagues, and communications service providers. The company has a strategic collaboration with T-Mobile US, Inc for the development of AI-native Scheduler with Link Adaptation software. The company was formerly known as Allmanna Telefon AB LM Ericsson and changed its name to Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ) in January 1926. Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ) was founded in 1876 and is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden.

financial_summary: Ericsson is a large-cap technology business with a $34.2B market cap on $23.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -4% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +2.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 20% against a 9% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 41%.

The business throws off $3.0B in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.15× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 8.8% (above the risk-free rate).
The 6 covering analysts target $9.52 on average, 10% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 20% clears the cost of capital of 9.0% by 11pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.36).
It runs a 41% gross margin and converts 13% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.15x.
ROE of 26% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 10pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.1B.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -3.5% over 3 years and -0.9% over 5 years, so the decline is deepening.
At current returns, reinvesting 26% of profits supports about 5.3% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 3.1% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 24.8% on average.
Analysts expect -3.8% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 12%.
It returns 2.8% a year to shareholders (3.0% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 13 consecutive years, raising it 8.3% a year over the last five.
